title: Tempeh Peanut Buddha Bowls
seoTitle: Tempeh Peanut Buddha Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Pan-crisped tempeh and edamame over rice with a peanut-lime sauce
subtitle: Pan-crisped tempeh and edamame over rice with a peanut-lime sauce
description: Crumbled tempeh pan-crisps until deeply browned, then joins edamame, shredded carrot, and cabbage over rice with a peanut-lime sauce. It is a vegetarian bowl built to actually hold up as a full dinner.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse brown rice and cook according to package directions. Fluff with a fork and hold covered.

steps.title: Crisp the tempeh
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add crumbled tempeh and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply browned and crisp at the edges. Stir in 2 tablespoons soy sauce in the last minute.

steps.title: Build the peanut-lime sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk peanut butter, remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, lime juice, honey, ginger, and garlic in a bowl until smooth, adding a splash of warm water to loosen it to a pourable consistency.

steps.title: Warm the edamame
steps.instruction: Steam or microwave edamame with a splash of water 3–4 minutes until hot. Toss with a pinch of salt.

steps.title: Hold everything separately
steps.instruction: Keep tempeh and rice covered and warm; keep shredded carrot, cabbage, and green onions cold and separate so the slaw stays crisp.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Layer rice, crisped tempeh, edamame, carrot, and cabbage in each bowl. Drizzle with peanut-lime sauce and finish with green onions and sesame seeds if using.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover crisped tempeh and peanut-lime sauce — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool tempeh peanut buddha bowls and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Freeze tempeh for 10 minutes before crumbling — it holds together better under a knife when firm.
Rookie tip: Don't skip the browning step; pale tempeh tastes bitter, well-browned tempeh tastes nutty and savory.
Add sriracha or chili crisp to the sauce for crews who want heat.
tonightSpread: Sides: Cucumber salad, extra lime wedges
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool tempeh peanut buddha bowls in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Sauce keeps separately up to a week — thin with water before reusing.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tempeh browns up hearty and savory instead of tasting like a meat substitute, and the peanut sauce means nobody treats this as a side dish.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: cook tempeh and rice up to two days ahead. Storage: keep tempeh, rice, and slaw vegetables in separate containers up to 4 days; store sauce separately. Reheating: warm tempeh and rice together, then add cold slaw and sauce.
substitutions: Use extra-firm tofu instead of tempeh.
Use almond butter instead of peanut butter for a nut allergy swap (still contains tree nuts).
Use quinoa instead of rice for extra protein.

adaptable.note: Use tamari (check soy-free brands separately) or coconut aminos.
